paragraphs: Rabbi Yaakov, son of Rav Yehudah bar Yechezkel.
Mentioned in Bamidbar Rabbah 14:3 and Midrash Tehillim 24:10. Hyman says that, without doubt, the name should read Rav Yitzchak: it had been abbreviated ר״י and was expanded to Rabbi Yaakov.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The intended Rav Yitzchak and mistaken Rabbi Yaakov are Hyman’s own explanation of ר״י. The read-only Midrash Tehillim 24:10 lookup returned a reference error; no confirmation is claimed from it.

The complete checked Bamidbar Rabbah 14:3 passage names Rabbi Yaakov son of Rav Yehudah bar Yechezkel; the complete checked Midrash Tehillim chapter 24 paragraph likewise names Rabbi Yaakov son of Rav Yehudah. The positive chapter 24 witness is distinct from the previously noted failed lookup at exact 24:10. Hyman’s “without doubt” and “should read Rav Yitzchak” retain their emphatic force as his proposed correction, not an emendation adopted here.
